details:
What does it do & Benefits:

This project identifies three key geological sites on Earth—the Atacama Desert (Chile), Mauna Loa (Hawaii), and Icelandic Lava Tubes—that mirror Lunar and Martian environments. From a civil engineering perspective, this project provides a cost-effective blueprint for testing structural foundations, 3D-printed regolith bricks, and natural radiation-shielded underground shelters before launching human missions.

Intended impact :

Testing infrastructure directly on the Moon or Mars is expensive and risky. Using Earth analog sites reduces mission costs, improves astronaut safety, and accelerates sustainable habitat construction for future space settlement.

Tools & Software used :

Microsoft PowerPoint (for presentation design), Google Drive (for hosting), and NASA Space Apps Challenge geological resources
